is_anopheles.evidence: The study evaluated wild Anopheles arabiensis and laboratory-reared Anopheles gambiae Kisumu strain (page 1, 6, 7).

reports_target_markers.evidence: Tested for the kdr L1014S (Vgsc L995S) mutation using a TaqMan qPCR assay (page 7, 10, 15).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 7 on page 15 and text on pages 10-11 report kdr L1014S genotype counts for wild-caught An. arabiensis (N=88: 0 RRe, 0 RSe, 88 SSe).

african_field_population.evidence: Wild An. arabiensis mosquitoes were collected as larvae from Lower Moshi, Tanzania and reared to adults (page 6, 7).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study reporting experimental hut trials and laboratory characterization of vector mosquitoes (page 1-3).

sub_country_location.evidence: Collections were made at Pasua (S03°22.764' E037°20.793') in Lower Moshi, Tanzania (page 6).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Field trial and mosquito collections were conducted from June 2019 to August 2019 (page 8).

duplicate_risk.evidence: Primary field study conducted in 2019 with no textual evidence of sample overlap with external public databases or prior publications.

supplement.evidence: Genotype frequency/count data for the field-collected mosquitoes are fully provided in Table 7 of the main text.

assessment.summary: This GLP-compliant study evaluated two candidate LLINs (SafeNet NF and SafeNet LLIN) in experimental huts against wild pyrethroid-resistant An. arabiensis in Pasua, Lower Moshi, Tanzania in 2019. Genotyping of wild-caught An. arabiensis (N=88) confirmed 100% SSe (homozygous susceptible) status for the Vgsc L1014S (L995S) mutation, while CDC bottle bioassays with PBO confirmed metabolic resistance mechanism involvement.
